rules.text:
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Rival plays a Unit with [ADRENALINE], which allows it to attack the turn it’s played. But a friendly Unit’s card text reads “Rival Units can't attack the turn they're played.” The preventing of the attack takes precedence, so the rival Unit can’t attack this turn.

2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit has 2 power. An effect reduces its power by 3. The Unit has -1 power, but is treated as having 0 power when attacking, fighting, or when a card effect references its power. If it then gains +2 power, that Unit has 1 power. The order of these effects being applied does not alter this outcome.

rules.title: A max Gig is any Gig die at its highest possible value.
rules.text:
6.3.2. A max Gig is any Gig die at its highest possible value.

> **EXAMPLE:** A d4 has four sides with possible values of 1, 2, 3, and 4. If its current value is 4, then it’s a max Gig.

rules.title: The highest value on a die is always equal to its number of sides, and the lowest value on a die is always 1.
rules.text:
6.3.3. The highest value on a die is always equal to its number of sides, and the lowest value on a die is always 1. This is true even if the specific die represents the number differently.

> **EXAMPLE:** If the faces of your d10 are labelled 0-9, the 0 represents “10” and is considered the highest value, while the 1 is considered the lowest value.

rules.title: A Gig’s value cannot be adjusted to the value it already has.
rules.text:
6.4.5. A Gig’s value cannot be adjusted to the value it already has. If an effect tells you to do so, the effect fails.

> **EXAMPLE:** If a Gig is at a min value, it cannot be changed to its min value by an effect. You may choose it for an effect that could adjust it to a min, but nothing would happen.

rules.title: A value-pair is 2 dice with the same value in the same Gig area.
rules.text: 6.5. A value-pair is 2 dice with the same value in the same Gig area.

rules.title: A Gig can only count towards a single value-pair at a time.
rules.text:
6.5.1. A Gig can only count towards a single value-pair at a time.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit’s card text reads “Draw 1 for each friendly value-pair of Gigs.” And your Gig area contains three Gig dice with the same value: a d4, d6, and d8. The d4 and d6 may be counted as a value-pair, and then there are no more Gigs to pair with the d8. So, there is exactly one friendly value-pair of Gigs. Draw 1 card.

rules.text: 10.1.3. When an effect refers to “this card,” “this Unit,” “this Legend,” “this Gear,” or another similar phrase, it refers to the source of that effect unless another rule or effect says otherwise.

rules.title: If you control the source of an effect, it is considered “your” effect.
rules.text: 10.1.4. If you control the source of an effect, it is considered “your” effect. You are the one who resolves it.

rules.title: To “resolve” an effect, follow the instructions of that effect in the order they appear.
rules.text: 10.2. To “resolve” an effect, follow the instructions of that effect in the order they appear.

rules.title: Always resolve as much of an effect as possible.
rules.text: 10.2.1. Always resolve as much of an effect as possible. See GOLDEN RULES > Resolve as Much as Possible.

rules.title: If an effect instructs both players to act at the same time, the turn player performs their actions first, followed b…
rules.text: 10.2.2. If an effect instructs both players to act at the same time, the turn player performs their actions first, followed by their Rival.

rules.title: Once an effect starts resolving, you cannot play cards, activate effects, or resolve other pending effects until the…
rules.text: 10.2.3. Once an effect starts resolving, you cannot play cards, activate effects, or resolve other pending effects until the current effect finishes resolving.

rules.title: Effects cannot interrupt the activation or resolution of other effects.
rules.text: 10.2.4. Effects cannot interrupt the activation or resolution of other effects. If an effect triggers in the middle of an activation or resolution, it becomes “pending resolution.” See EFFECTS > Pending Resolution.

rules.title: After an effect resolves, perform any required rule processing before resolving a new one or taking any actions.
rules.text: 10.2.5. After an effect resolves, perform any required rule processing before resolving a new one or taking any actions.

rules.title: An effect may include conditions.
rules.text: 10.3. An effect may include conditions. A “condition” is a requirement that must be true for an effect to apply, become pending, and resolve. (Conditions are often “if” or “when” clauses.)

rules.title: If a condition is false, do not apply its corresponding effect.
rules.text: 10.3.1. If a condition is false, do not apply its corresponding effect.

rules.title: A condition is not a cost unless it is specifically within a cost.
rules.text: 10.3.2. A condition is not a cost unless it is specifically within a cost. See Cost.

rules.title: A condition within an effect’s resolution is checked when that part of the effect resolves.
rules.text: 10.3.3. A condition within an effect’s resolution is checked when that part of the effect resolves.

rules.title: An effect is “invalid” if it cannot apply according to its text, the game rules, or the current game state.
rules.text: 10.6. An effect is “invalid” if it cannot apply according to its text, the game rules, or the current game state.

rules.title: If all of an effect is invalid, ignore that effect.
rules.text: 10.6.1. If all of an effect is invalid, ignore that effect.

rules.title: If part of an effect is invalid, ignore the invalid part and resolve as much of the remaining effect as possible.
rules.text: 10.6.2. If part of an effect is invalid, ignore the invalid part and resolve as much of the remaining effect as possible.

rules.title: Even if an effect is invalid, it is still considered an effect on the card.
rules.text: 10.6.3. Even if an effect is invalid, it is still considered an effect on the card.

rules.title: If an effect becomes invalid after it activates or becomes pending, still resolve as much of the effect as possible.
rules.text: 10.10. If an effect becomes invalid after it activates or becomes pending, still resolve as much of the effect as possible.

rules.title: If resolving a pending effect requires information about a game piece that is no longer valid, use the information fr…
rules.text: 10.10.1. If resolving a pending effect requires information about a game piece that is no longer valid, use the information from when the piece was last valid.

rules.title: If an effect instructs a player to choose, select, or otherwise make a choice, that choice is made when the effect in…
rules.text: 10.31. If an effect instructs a player to choose, select, or otherwise make a choice, that choice is made when the effect instructs the player to make that choice.

rules.title: If an effect requires a choice and no legal choice can be made, that choice is not made.
rules.text: 10.31.1. If an effect requires a choice and no legal choice can be made, that choice is not made.

rules.title: If an effect requires you to choose a specific number of targets, you must choose that number of targets.
rules.text: 10.31.2. If an effect requires you to choose a specific number of targets, you must choose that number of targets. If you can’t, choose as many valid targets as possible up to that number instead.

rules.title: If an effect requires a player to choose a number, that player must choose a non-negative whole number.
rules.text: 10.31.3. If an effect requires a player to choose a number, that player must choose a non-negative whole number.

rules.title: If multiple choices are required while resolving an effect, make those choices in the order written.
rules.text: 10.32. If multiple choices are required while resolving an effect, make those choices in the order written.

rules.title: [Star] Street Cred
rules.text: 11.2. ### [Star] Street Cred

rules.title: Your “Street Cred” is the sum of all Gig dice values in the friendly Gig area.
rules.text: 11.2.1. Your “Street Cred” is the sum of all Gig dice values in the friendly Gig area.

rules.title: The [Star] symbol is shorthand for Street Cred.
rules.text: 11.2.2. The [Star] symbol is shorthand for Street Cred.

rules.title: When you have no Gigs in your Gig area you have Null ( - ) Street Cred.
rules.text: 11.2.3. When you have no Gigs in your Gig area you have Null ( - ) Street Cred. Null does not count as having 0.

rules.title: Lag
Lag is a condition applied to Units when they enter the field.
rules.text: 11.3.1. Lag is a condition applied to Units when they enter the field. Units with Lag are also called “lagging.”

rules.title: Lagging Units can’t attack.
rules.text: 11.3.1.1. Lagging Units can’t attack.

rules.title: Lagging Units can’t activate [Spend Icon] effects.
rules.text: 11.3.1.2. Lagging Units can’t activate [Spend Icon] effects.

rules.title: At the end of each turn, all Units lose the “Lag” condition.
rules.text: 11.3.2. At the end of each turn, all Units lose the “Lag” condition.

rules.title: Play
To play a card, reveal it, pay its cost, and then follow the rules for playing that specific card type detailed in {C…
rules.text: 11.4.1. To play a card, reveal it, pay its cost, and then follow the rules for playing that specific card type detailed in CARD TYPES.

rules.title: If you can’t pay for or follow the rules for playing the card, you cannot play it.
rules.text: 11.4.1.1. If you can’t pay for or follow the rules for playing the card, you cannot play it. It’s considered “invalid” to play.

rules.title: If you play or attempt to play an invalid card, undo the play attempt and return the game to the previous legal game…
rules.text: 11.4.1.2. If you play or attempt to play an invalid card, undo the play attempt and return the game to the previous legal game state as much as possible.

rules.title: You can only play cards from your hand unless an effect instructs otherwise.
rules.text: 11.4.2. You can only play cards from your hand unless an effect instructs otherwise.

rules.title: Effects that allow a player to play a card follows the normal rules for playing that card unless the effect instructs…
rules.text: 11.4.3. Effects that allow a player to play a card follows the normal rules for playing that card unless the effect instructs otherwise.

rules.title: Draw
“Draw” is a game action in which you move the top card of your deck to your hand.
rules.text: 11.5.1. “Draw” is a game action in which you move the top card of your deck to your hand.

rules.title: When an effect says “Draw X” (where X is a number), take the draw action X number of times.
rules.text: 11.5.2. When an effect says “Draw X” (where X is a number), take the draw action X number of times. Literally, it means “move the top card of your deck to your hand, X individual times.”

rules.title: When you “Draw X,” draw each card individually.
rules.text: 11.5.2.1. When you “Draw X,” draw each card individually. Do not take multiple cards from the top of your deck at once.

rules.title: When you “Draw up to X,” choose the number of cards you will draw, then draw exactly that number of cards.
rules.text: 11.5.2.2. When you “Draw up to X,” choose the number of cards you will draw, then draw exactly that number of cards.

rules.title: If you attempt to draw more cards than remain in your deck, it counts as drawing from an empty deck.
rules.text: 11.5.2.3. If you attempt to draw more cards than remain in your deck, it counts as drawing from an empty deck. See GAME OVERVIEW > Lose Conditions.

rules.title: [PLAY]
The [PLAY] trigger is shorthand for “When you play this card, [...]”
rules.text: 11.20.1. The [PLAY] trigger is shorthand for “When you play this card, [...]”

rules.title: The effect attached to the [PLAY] trigger enters pending when you meet all the requirements when playing that card type.
rules.text: 11.20.2. The effect attached to the [PLAY] trigger enters pending when you meet all the requirements when playing that card type. See CARD TYPES.

faqs.question: Does 0 count as an even number?
Can I choose to increase a Gig by 0?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it does not count as "adjusting" a Gig for effects triggered by "adjusting a Gig."

faqs.question: Can I adjust a rival Gig?

decisions.order: 2.3,10.2,10.3.3: resolve increase first, then current any-controlled-Gig >=8 check, even after zero/no target. No intervening action.
decisions.targets: A Gig means either controller; Industrial FAQ confirms rival target. A different friendly Gig can satisfy the second clause. Fixer dice excluded.
decisions.zero: 2.8 and Industrial FAQ: 0 legal, no adjustment/value-change fact; later clause remains. Forced target/zero choices do not create strategic pauses.
decisions.bounds: 6.3–6.4: current value and die faces1..max, exact0..min(4,max-current), no clamping.
decisions.parity: 2.10.2,5.11.4.1,11.2 and Field Operator FAQ No to 0: empty area is Null, never even. Numeric Street Cred0 is unreachable with positive controlled Gig faces. Test Null and legal positive even/odd.
decisions.play: 4.6–4.7,11.20.2: payment, ready field entry/Lag, then ordinary PLAY pending/resolution; automatic conditional draw at resolution.
decisions.source: Industrial6 printings (Dudar/Duder artist spelling retained verbatim), Field Operator5 printings. All4 errata read; neither card affected.
